market.what: extra boron-removal step in seawater RO (2nd pass at high pH, boron-selective resins), world
market.method: 109M m3/d contracted desal x ~50% SWRO (est.) x 0.8 online x 365 = ~16 bn m3/yr; ~40% needs a boron step (est.) = 6.4 bn m3 x ~$0.07/m3 extra = ~$450M/yr

value.logic: binder polishing a split stream instead of pH-10 2nd pass (caustic, acid, ~0.2-0.3 kWh/m3, brine) saves ~$0.035/m3 x 6.4 bn m3 = ~$220M/yr; 2-pass total $0.45-0.55/m3 today
value.revenue_logic: ~4% of ~$450M boron-step spend by yr 7 as resin via licensee/toll maker
value.margin_logic: specialty chelating resin vs NMG resins (DuPont, Purolite, Mitsubishi); price pressure from Chinese resin makers

trend.drivers: Gulf/N. Africa SWRO megaprojects; desal water for irrigation (Spain, Israel) needs B <=0.3-0.5 mg/L; reports 9.1%/yr desal market

competition.notes: groups capped at 200. No startup found; strongest new idea is boron-selective electrosorption (U Michigan/Rice, Nature Water 2025, academic). Incumbent fix is membranes + pH swing, sold inside big EPC tenders

lab.synth: 1-2 step custom (TRIS-type polyol binder from catalog TRIS) + grafting to resin bead
lab.test: batch + column on real or synthetic SWRO permeate (0.8-1.5 mg/L B, pH 7-8), regeneration cycles; boron by ICP-OES/ICP-MS (EPA 200.7) at a university lab
lab.logic: 6 wk synth ($6-8k) + 6 wk grafting/3 variants ($20k) + 6 wk tests; ~200 samples x $32-80 (UConn, USF) = ~$10k + labor

sale.gates: NSF/ANSI 61 or local potable approval; 6-12 mo pilot at an SWRO plant; design-in to EPC tenders
